senses.gloss: m. (contr. of איסהר, cmp. איסתירא, an adapt. of assarius = as) As, a Roman coin, usu. 1/24 of a Denar (v. Zuckerm. Talm. Gew. p. 22 sq.), called א׳ האיטלקי Italian As.
units: Kidd. I, 1; a. fr.—Y. ibid. I, 58ᵈ הא׳ אחד מכ״ד וכ׳ the As is 1/24 of the silver Denar.—Trnsf. coin.
<cite ref="Taanit 19b:2">Taan. 19ᵇ</cite> <he>מדלית א׳</he> because there was a scarcity of coin.—Pl. <he>אִיסָרִין</he>.
Y. Maas. Sh. IV, 55ᵇ top.—Chald.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 12a:11">Kidd. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>איסורי</he> read <he>אִיסָרֵי</he>. [<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 42:4">Gen. R. s. 42</cite> <he>א׳ לשם אלסר</he> the Assar received its name from Elasar (<cite ref="Genesis 14:1">Gen. XIV, 1</cite>), comment.; v. however next w.]
